title: U.S. Senate · New Jersey

context.text: Incumbent Cory Booker (D) ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 100% of the vote (587,980 votes).
Justin Murphy won a four-way Republican primary on June 2, 2026 with 33.4% of the vote (82,272 votes), ahead of Richard Tabor (29.2%), Alex Zdan (26.8%), and Robert Lebovics (10.7%).
Cook Political Report, Decision Desk HQ, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rated the general election Solid/Safe Democratic as of September 2026.
Eduardo Castillo, who did not run in the Democratic primary, is listed by Ballotpedia as a write-in candidate carrying a Democratic Party label in the general election.

candidates.name: Cory Booker
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the June 2 Democratic primary

summary.text: Cory Booker is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from New Jersey, in office since October 2013. A Stanford, Oxford and Yale Law graduate, he started a legal-services nonprofit in Newark, served on the Newark City Council (1998-2002) and as Mayor of Newark (2006-2013), and ran for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary and chairs the Senate Democrats' Strategic Communications Committee.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C., in 1969 and grew up in northern New Jersey.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science (1991) and a master's in sociology (1992) from Stanford University, where he played varsity football; as a Rhodes Scholar, earned a graduate degree in history at the University of Oxford (1994), and received a J.D. from Yale Law School in 1997.

After law school he moved to Newark and, according to his Senate biography, started a nonprofit providing legal services to low-income families; he also worked as a staff attorney at the Urban Justice Center and as program coordinator of the Newark Youth Project.
Elected to the Newark City Council at 29 and served from 1998 to 2002; served as Mayor of Newark from 2006 to 2013.
Won a special election to the U.S. Senate in October 2013, was re-elected to a full term in 2014 and re-elected in 2020.
Announced a campaign for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination on February 1, 2019, and suspended it on January 13, 2020.

Serves on the Senate Judiciary, Foreign Relations, Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, and Small Business committees; elected chairman of the Senate Democrats' Strategic Communications Committee without opposition on December 3, 2024.

His Senate biography cites his work on the First Step Act, a criminal justice law enacted in December 2018. On March 31, 2025, he began a Senate floor speech that lasted 25 hours and five minutes, the longest in Senate history.
According to his Senate biography, he lives in Newark's Central Ward.

record.text: Sits on the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Commodities, Derivatives, Risk Management, and Trade), the Committee on the Judiciary (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights), and the Committee on Foreign Relations for the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

On March 31–April 1, 2025, held the Senate floor for 25 hours and 5 minutes, breaking the record for the longest individual floor speech in Senate history (previously held by Sen. Strom Thurmond's 24-hour, 18-minute speech in 1957). The speech criticized policies of the Trump administration's first weeks in office.

With Rep. Adriano Espaillat, introduced the Community Mental Wellness Worker Training Act, which would create a competitive federal grant program to help behavioral health organizations train community mental wellness workers to expand access to culturally and linguistically responsive mental health services.

candidates.name: Justin Murphy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2 Republican primary with 33.4% in a four-candidate field

summary.text: Justin Murphy is a Tabernacle, New Jersey attorney and U.S. Navy veteran who won the 2026 Republican Senate primary. He served a term on the Tabernacle Township Committee and has been active in Burlington County Republican politics since 1988. He previously ran for the Republican Senate nomination in 2024, finishing third, and his campaign pledge calls for a flat income tax and abolishing the federal Department of Education.

background.text: According to InsiderNJ, he was raised in the Pinelands of Southern New Jersey and lives in Tabernacle.
Enlisted in the U.S. Navy at age 17 and served a four-year term aboard the USS Comte De Grasse (DD 974), including six months in the Persian Gulf during the Iran-Iraq war; honorably discharged.
Elected to the Tabernacle Township Committee in November 2000 and served a three-year term; Ballotpedia lists him as a former deputy mayor of Tabernacle.

Active in Republican politics since 1988: vice president of the Burlington County Young Republicans (1994-1997), a member of the county committee (1996-2000) and president of the Tabernacle Republican Organization (1998-2000).
A practicing attorney since 2006, with a practice covering estate, real estate, contracts, energy consulting and EB-5 economic development; his campaign website says he is self-employed.
Ran for the Republican U.S. Senate nomination in 2024 and lost, finishing third with 11.3% of the vote.
Won the June 2, 2026 Republican Senate primary over a field of four.

priorities.text: Campaign platform calls for abolishing the IRS and the Internal Revenue Code and replacing them with a flat income tax of 10–12%, eliminating the capital gains tax and estate/death taxes.

Supports completing the southern border wall, securing the northern border, withholding federal aid from self-declared sanctuary cities/states, and stationing the U.S. military on the southern border.
Supports abolishing the federal Department of Education and dividing its roughly $100 billion budget among local school boards for public education funding and school-voucher programs.

positions.summary: Calls for abolishing the IRS and current tax code in favor of a flat income tax of 10–12%, and eliminating the capital gains and estate taxes entirely.
Supports completing the southern border wall, securing the northern border, expanding 287(g) state/local immigration enforcement partnerships, and stationing the U.S. military on the border.
Describes himself as pro-life, with exceptions for the life of the mother and cases of rape/incest; opposes taxpayer funding of abortion and supports parental notification requirements.
Says he will oppose any government attempt to restrict Second Amendment rights and supports Constitutional Carry.
Supports school choice and competition between schools, and would redirect federal Department of Education funding to local school boards including for voucher programs.

Says he opposes government-run healthcare, instead proposing universal Health Savings Accounts, a national health-insurance marketplace across state lines, and anti-fraud enforcement in Medicare and Medicaid.

summary.text: Veronica Fernandez is a Morris County small-business owner and former insurance underwriter running as the End the Corruption! Party nominee, campaigning primarily on campaign-finance reform. She has run for office several times, including the 2020 U.S. Senate race and a 2023 General Assembly race.

background.text: Born in Franklin, New Jersey; earned a high school diploma from Sussex County Vo-Tech and attended County College of Morris for undergraduate study.
Worked 20 years as a licensed property/casualty and health insurance underwriter in New Jersey.

Co-owns and operates a small commercial electrical contracting business with her husband, a Navy veteran and electrician; in her survey response she describes experience owning and operating a union (IBEW Local 102) shop.

Volunteer coordinator for the Interfaith Council of Homeless Families in Morris County for seven years and a foster parent, according to her survey response; Ballotpedia notes an affiliation with the League of Women Voters.

Ran for U.S. Senate in 2020 (Of, By, For! Party; 0.7%), withdrew from the 2022 race for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, and ran for New Jersey General Assembly District 24 in 2023 as the End The Corruption! Party candidate (8.1%).

priorities.text: Says her platform centers on electoral reform, including a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United v. FEC.
priorities.quote: My platform centers on electoral reform. The SCOTUS ruling on Citizens United in 2010 opened the flood gates for the "legal" corruption of our candidates, elections, and policies. I fully support a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United.

priorities.text: Supports Medicare for All, arguing private insurance is structurally unable to cover ongoing healthcare needs.
Supports abolishing ICE and closing immigration detention centers, and creating a fast-tracked path to citizenship for people without more than a misdemeanor conviction.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All, saying insurance-based healthcare cannot adequately cover maintenance care.
Supports abolishing ICE, closing detention centers, and a fast-tracked path to citizenship for immigrants without more than a misdemeanor conviction.

summary.text: Joanne Kuniansky is the Socialist Workers Party's nominee for U.S. Senate. She has been the party's candidate in a series of New Jersey elections since 2021, including the 2024 U.S. Senate race, in which she received 0.2% of the vote.

background.text: According to a candidate statement from her 2021 campaign, she had worked in oil refineries, railroads and meat packing, and at that time was a Walmart deli worker.

Ran as the Socialist Workers Party candidate for governor in 2021, for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District in 2022, for New Jersey State Senate District 33 in 2023 (2.9%) and for governor in 2025.
Ran previously as the Socialist Workers Party's candidate for U.S. Senate in New Jersey in 2024, winning 9,806 votes (0.2%).

candidates.name: Eduardo Castillo
candidates.ballotNote: Write-in candidate carrying a Democratic Party label; did not appear on the Democratic primary ballot

summary.text: Eduardo Castillo is a Monmouth County retail worker running a write-in general-election campaign built around workers' rights, banking reform, and family-support policy. He ran for the New Jersey General Assembly in 2025.

background.text: Describes himself as a Monmouth County resident and retail worker who has held more than six retail jobs.
background.quote: I'm Eduardo Castillo, a resident of Monmouth County, partner to a very lovely girl, and retail worker, just trying to make ends meet, like everyone else.

background.text: Ran for New Jersey General Assembly District 13 in the November 4, 2025 general election, which was won by two Republican incumbents.

priorities.text: Supports just-cause firing protections, a $31 minimum wage indexed to inflation, at least 15 paid vacation days per year, and paid leave after miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion.
Supports free school meals for all students, an increased child tax credit, and free childcare, pre-K, and four-year college for all.
Supports capping ATM fees at $2.00, capping credit card interest rates at 10%, and creating a public banking option.

positions.summary: Supports a $31 minimum wage indexed to inflation.
Supports free childcare, pre-K, and four-year college for all.

researchNotes: Cory Booker has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his campaign website (corybooker.com) is fundraising-only with no published issues platform, so his priorities/positions sections rely on recent official Senate actions rather than campaign statements; per the research brief his federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Veronica Fernandez and Eduardo Castillo's entries rely entirely on their Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses. Joanne Kuniansky has published no detailed 2026 platform beyond her party affiliation and 2024 election result; her entry is marked minimal. Biography gaps: Eduardo Castillo and Joanne Kuniansky have very little public biographical information beyond Ballotpedia; Murphy's local-office title differs between Ballotpedia (deputy mayor) and InsiderNJ (Township Committee member), and both are given.
